'''Hermas Walter McFarland''' (March 11, 1870 – September 21, 1935) was an American professional [[baseball]] player. He played all or part of five seasons in [[Major League Baseball]] for the [[Louisville Colonels]] (1896), [[Cincinnati Reds]] (1898), [[Chicago White Sox]] (1901–02) and [[Baltimore Orioles (1901–02)|Baltimore Orioles]]/[[New York Highlanders]] (1902–03), primarily as an [[outfielder]].

Born in [[Des Moines, Iowa]], McFarland was a member of the White Sox team that won the 1901 [[American League]] [[pennant (sports)|pennant]]. In 5 seasons he played in 352 games and had 1,278 at bats, 204 runs, 340 hits, 61 doubles, 28 triples, 13 home runs, 167 RBI, 64 stolen bases, 175 walks, .266 batting average, .362 on-base percentage, .388 slugging percentage, 496 total bases and 26 sacrifice hits.

He died in [[Richmond, Virginia]] at the age of 65.
